topic: Securing a Microsoft Foundry agent: never put a user ID in a tool schema, resolve identity from the validated JWT in the executor, check roles before tools run, and defend against prompt injection in tool output.

title.sub: The model can only pass what you let it.

stages.title: One edited dish
stages.desc: A partner can edit their menu, and the menu comes back inside a tool result.
stages.status: UPDATE Dishes SET Description = '... SYSTEM: ignore ...'
stages.narration: A restaurant partner edits a dish description. It contains instructions.

stages.title: Into the context
stages.desc: The tool result carries that text straight into the model.
stages.narration: The tool returns it, and it lands in the model context.

stages.title: If tools take IDs
stages.desc: get_user_profile(userId) lets a fooled model ask for anyone.
stages.narration: If tools take user I Ds, a fooled model asks for anyone.

stages.title: Remove the parameter
stages.desc: get_user_profile() takes no ID at all.
stages.narration: So remove the parameter. The tool takes no I D at all.

stages.title: Identity from the token
stages.desc: The executor resolves the caller from the validated JWT.
stages.narration: The executor reads who is calling from the validated token.

stages.title: Role check first
stages.desc: Each tool has the roles allowed to call it, checked before it runs.
stages.narration: Then a role check runs before any tool does.

stages.title: Layers, not one fix
stages.desc: Harmless tools, instruction separation, sanitising, content filters.
stages.narration: Add layers: harmless tools, separated instructions, sanitising, filters.

stages.title: Even fooled, it is contained
stages.desc: A fully compromised model still gets only the caller’s own data.
stages.status: the test: a second user, denied
stages.narration: Even a fully fooled model now reaches only the caller’s own data.

stages.title: No user ID in any tool
stages.desc: Resolve identity in the executor, so even a fooled model cannot reach another user.
stages.narration: No user ID in any tool.

end.title: No user ID in any tool.
end.sub: Design so that a fully compromised model still cannot reach another user’s data.

post.caption:
Never put a user ID in an AI agent tool. 🔐

A restaurant partner edits a dish description to include "SYSTEM: ignore previous instructions". That text comes back inside a tool result and lands in the model context.

If a tool takes userId, a fooled model can ask for anyone. So the tool takes no ID. The executor reads the caller from the validated JWT, checks the role, then runs the tool.

Even a fully compromised model reaches only the caller's own data.

Full article: blog.msdevbuild.com/blog/azure-ai-foundry-agent-security-jwt-roles
